rv.q: This is a staging of exceptional clarity and insight, and it pulses with life and urgency.
McKellen's work is towering, poignant and fearsome as it marks Lear's faltering imperiousness, punctuated by sudden piercing shafts of clarity and self-awareness.
Whatever its inconsistencies and imperfections, this production still dazzles, McKellen shimmering brightest at its dark, tormented heart.
What we have instead is a close up on the personal, and here the production takes flight.
Following Andrew Scott's memorable Hamlet, this captivating Lear sets the bar for those to come.
Ian McKellen’s latest effort fully justifies his reputation and all of the hype.
Yet for a play about the slow death of the chief protagonist, it will leave you stubbornly unmoved.

cn.t: McKellen delivers a magnificent, majestic performance in his return to the title role, capturing the character's fractured descent with shattering acuity in Munby's splendid modern-dress production from Chichester.
